attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: In context, 'that' refers to generalizing beyond the training space when handling outliers. The normalised proposition keeps this, and the claim is causal.

contract.note: The contract reads 'inherent problem' as an intrinsic obstacle, not universal failure. That is a fair, ordinary reading. 'Localism' is undefined, so the result depends on how it is made operational.

evidence.note: The Xu et al. theory paper (2021) shows ReLU MLPs extrapolate poorly for nonlinear targets. It also finds that diverse training data and task-specific architecture enable extrapolation. It does not isolate a 'localism' mechanism.

reviews.rationale: The only item is context. It documents some structural limits on extrapolation, but also conditions under which networks extrapolate well. It neither isolates nor refutes localism as an inherent cause across neural networks. The packet does not meet the support or contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'lousy at outliers' and 'often' absurd behaviour in unusual circumstances. It does not overstate the claim as universal failure.

contract.note: The plain reading is a recurring weakness on unusual or modestly altered inputs, judged on challenge sets, for 2024 up to the post date. This is fair and ordinary, not stretched for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: The July 2024 version of the AIW study ran 30 or more trials per variation. Many models had very low success and large swings on a simple altered problem. GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus did better but were still imperfect.
An ICML 2024 benchmark finds severe out-of-distribution weakness in adversarially robust vision models. That scope is narrower than the claim, so it is context only.

In materials science, models do well on most heuristic out-of-distribution tasks, but those tasks are mostly interpolation. Models do poorly on inputs truly outside the training domain. This qualifies the claim but does not contradict it.

reviews.rationale: e1 is a documented, repeated-trial evaluation from before the post. It shows substantial failures across many models on a simple, slightly varied reasoning problem, which meets the support condition. e3 shows that apparent out-of-distribution success often reflects interpolation, so it does not show reliable handling of real outliers. No packet item meets the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Marcus reposts his own tweet and endorses it.

semantics.note: The group is defined only by an unobservable mental state (not understanding outliers), and the dollar figure is hyperbolic and possibly a typo. This is polemical framing, not a testable factual observation.

contract.note: The contract keeps $100M literal, which is faithful to the words. But it must identify an unnamed population and prove its misunderstanding, which cannot be measured. The result depends entirely on the evaluator choosing a group and a measure of 'burned'.

evidence.note: Reports a forecast of OpenAI's 2024 annual loss. That is a different measure, not realized spending, and it does not involve an identified group that 'doesn't understand'.
A 2021 Waymo blog post (company disclosure) on simulating rare events. It bears on understanding at one firm, but not on amounts or on the unnamed group.

reviews.rationale: 'Those who don't' is a rhetorical group defined by a mental state with no identifiable members. 'Burned' and 'similar amounts' have no stated basis. No evidence could tie specific spending to that group's misunderstanding, so the claim cannot be scored as an observation.

attribution.note: Marcus quotes his own tweet and endorses it in the post.

semantics.note: Dropping the rhetorical 'two groups' framing is reasonable. The causal core ('therefore struggle') is kept for both domains.

contract.note: The contract treats outlier handling as a contributing cause, not the only one, and requires a mechanism link in both domains. This is a fair, ordinary reading. 'Outlier' and 'high-level reasoning' are undefined.

evidence.note: June 2024 version: controlled perturbations cut accuracy by more than 30 points for all models. This partly supports the reasoning component, but the authors note some perturbations also make tasks harder.

A Waymo recall filed with NHTSA in 2024 traces a pole collision to map and perception conditions. It does not show the object was outside training coverage, so it does not establish the outlier mechanism.

reviews.rationale: The support condition requires a mechanism link in both reasoning and driving. e1 partly supports reasoning, with a difficulty confound. e2 does not tie the driving failure to outlier handling. Nothing meets the contradiction condition, so the claim as a whole is not settled.
